trigger: User accidentally activated MARK CAUGHT UP before reading the catch-up projection and explicitly asked for undo/reversibility.

observed.before: MARK CAUGHT UP overwrote field.catchup.seen.v01 with one browser-local timestamp and retained no predecessor.
observed.failure: The action did not mutate repository/canonical state, but it irreversibly discarded the browser's prior orientation boundary.

behavior: MARK CAUGHT UP pushes the previous local boundary before advancing it.
REWIND restores the preceding retained boundary.
If a mark predates history support and no predecessor exists, REWIND clears the mark and reopens the all-indexed-changes view.
History is bounded to 20 local boundaries.
No canonical FIELD state, Git history, manifest truth, CURRENT attention, or server-side read state is mutated by using the control.

distinctions: UNDO = inverse of a prior reversible domain mutation.
REWIND = move a retained context/history pointer without claiming canonical state changed.
REVERT = a new authorized compensating canonical/world action; provenance remains append-only.
semantic_promotion.root_default: Prefer previewable, branchable, reversible or explicitly compensatable operations when meaning permits; cheap local/context mutations must retain a lawful way back.

verification.public_surface: public-surface-check runs the reversibility selftest and existing FIELD browser smoke.
verification.human: On the same browser that has the accidental legacy mark, press REWIND once. Expected: the local caught-up mark clears and the catch-up projection becomes visible again; future marks retain exact previous local boundaries.

residue: A predecessor overwritten before this feature shipped cannot be reconstructed exactly; the only honest fallback is the unmarked/all-changes view.
REWIND is local orientation only. It does not rewind repository or world state.
stop: Do not turn this into global event sourcing or another history database. Promote reversible mechanics only where an actual interaction can lose meaningful local/domain state.
